audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the level chart was wrong in both layers: it read Skill/Skill/Skill/Akshan/Skill/Akshan/Akshan against the packet's Akshan/Sett/Sett/Sett/Sett/Sett/Sett, and the difficulty was set to 7/10 with an 8/10 carry threat on a lane Sett wins 53.29% of over 1610 games.
audit.why: The whys text already said Akshan takes Level 1 with Avengerang range and Sett takes every level after; the tokens said otherwise. Akshan never builds resistances, so an 8/10 carry threat overstates him badly.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Akshan / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett in both layers as one atomic paired group; diffRating to 5/10, carryRating to 6/10, and the three prose lines carrying those numbers brought with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown or range numbers anywhere, so 'engage when Heroic Swing is down' gave the player nothing to count.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s at 800 range, Avengerang reaches 850, Comeuppance is 100/85/70s at 2500 range, and The Show Stopper is 120/100/80s at 400 range. Going Rogue drops to a 2s cooldown at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into phases[0], [1], [2], [4], spikes[1] and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions were absent and one was fabricated. Absent: Going Rogue is camouflage (a vision problem you have no reveal for) and Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit. Fabricated: spikes[1] claimed The Show Stopper 'suppresses him through his E swing'.
audit.why: Riot's description of The Show Stopper says carry, slam, damage and a landing slow — it says nothing about suppression or about interrupting Heroic Swing, and the mirror audit flagged the same over-claim. Going Rogue carries the stealth flag and the passive the shield flag.
audit.corrected: Suppression claim removed from spikes[1] and replaced with what Riot actually describes; camouflage/vision requirement stated in dontsFull[2].d; the every-third-hit shield stated in dosFull[2].d.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Akshan on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Avengerang out-ranges your fists at 850 and chips you on every last-hit. Soak it with Pit Grit's missing-health regen and don't step up before Knuckle Down.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Akshan and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with Heroic Swing.
edits.after: Knuckle Down's move speed closes the 850 gap for two empowered punches. Trade short and step out before Heroic Swing is back at 18s.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Akshan burns Heroic Swing.
edits.after: Facebreaker is online at 16s — stun him into your minions, then double punch into Haymaker. A one-sided pull only slows.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Akshan has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: You walk him down now: Knuckle Down closes, Facebreaker is 16s, and the Grit banked off his poke cashes as a Haymaker a marksman cannot survive.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Akshan doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: Comeuppance is a long-range execute for teamfights, not a duel escape. The Show Stopper starts fights he cannot refuse — slam him into your minions.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Akshan. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker sticks you to him and he never buys resistances. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the trade — one Facebreaker on a marksman ends it.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Heroic Swing and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in unburstable while Akshan stays squishy. Haymaker's centre is true damage — his resistances never enter the maths at all.

edits.before: Akshan wastes Heroic Swing — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Every third hit shields him — force Dirty Fighting out, then commit.

edits.before: Dumping autos into Akshan with an empty grit bar and no E — your W hits like a pillow and he just out-trades you on cooldowns.
edits.after: Going Rogue is camouflage and rank 5 is a 2s cooldown — you need a Control Ward and a sweeper to see him, not just a ward line.

edits.before: Carry threat: 8/10. If Akshan gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and jungle play.
edits.after: Carry threat: 6/10. If Akshan gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and jungle play.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Heroic Swing and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Heroic Swing and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7/10, Akshan carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 5/10, Akshan carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: The Show Stopper turns their frontliner into a missile for your team — late game you flank, R the carry-adjacent tank, and let the slam chunk the backline. Akshan carry threat: 8/10 — end the game before he cashes it.
edits.after: The Show Stopper turns their frontliner into a missile for your team — late game you flank, R the carry-adjacent tank, and let the slam chunk the backline. Akshan carry threat: 6/10 — he never buys resistances.

edits.before: Comeuppance (R) is a long-range execute for teamfights, not a duel tool -- it won't save him from your engage. Keep pressuring: your R The Show Stopper suppresses him through his E swing and slams him into your minions for a kill.
edits.after: Comeuppance (R) is a 2500-range execute for teamfights, not a duel tool -- it won't save him from your engage. Keep pressuring: The Show Stopper carries him 400 units and slams him into your minions, and it is back every 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Akshan stays squishy and relies on E Heroic Swing to reposition -- if you land E Facebreaker mid-swing he's dead. You out-brawl him all game once you're on top of him; just don't get poked out before you engage.
edits.after: Akshan stays squishy and relies on Heroic Swing (18s at rank 1) to reposition -- punish him hard in that window. You out-brawl him all game once you're on top of him; just don't get poked out before you engage.

notes: This entry was inverted on all seven chart rows in both layers at once and rated the lane Tricky at 7/10 despite a 53.29% win rate. It also asserted that The Show Stopper suppresses Akshan through Heroic Swing; Riot's text supports neither the suppression nor the interrupt, so I removed it rather than restate it.
